page0.text:
The clock turns.
It's past 9 o'clock.
Two hours ago, I carried Sakura who had collapsed near the front door into the living room, as Tohsaka told me to.
My paralyzed brain finally started working.

page1.text:
"Hey, Shirou. Are you feeling better now?"
"Mm, I think I'm back to normal. Sorry for making you worry, Illya. To be honest, I don't have any memory of the last two hours, so I don't know what stupid stuff I did."

page2.text: "Hmm. You didn't really do anything. You came in carrying Sakura and held her hand the whole time while Rin was treating her. Once we knew that she just had a high fever, you sat on the floor."

page3.text:
"Oh. What about Tohsaka? I think she took Sakura to her bedroom."
"Rin was looking through the closet in the tatami room.
I bet she was looking for a change of clothes for Sakura. She came back all dirty, so we would need to change her before getting her to bed, right?"

page4.text:
...
I see.
That makes sense.
I'd have to stay in the living room, in that case.
"Hey. I'm going to change her, and you're a guy, so why are you coming with us?"
Tohsaka probably gave me such a warning.

page5.text:
"So I've been waiting here for 2 hours, huh. Even if I was confused, that's still..."
It makes me feel like an idiot.
Seriously, what's going on with me today?
There's so many things I should be thinking about.
Sakura's well-being after she collapsed from a fever.
The massive meal that the enemy had last night.

page7.text:
...No, I can think about those later.
Right now, I should be considering why Sakura was found outside the house, when she went to sleep next to—

page8.text:
...
I want to vomit.
My thoughts deny each other.
Two hours of lost time.
That's how long I thought about that problem to the point of not wanting to anymore, my body reminds me...

page9.text:
"Shirou. Don't try to remember things that you can't remember.
You didn't forget it. It's just gone. When you try to dig up something that doesn't exist anymore, all you'll find is pain."
"Huh...? Illya?"
"...Never mind. I was just talking to myself. Forget it."
Illya looks away and goes quiet.

page10.text:
A few minutes pass.
Around the time the hand on the clock points to ten...
"Thanks for waiting. Sakura's awake."
Tohsaka came in and said it like it was no big deal.

page11.text:
"...Tohsaka. Is Sakura all right?"
"Who knows? You should be asking her, not me. I don't think you should hear it from me."
"...All right. I'm going to see her."
I stand up.
I leave Illya and Tohsaka in the living room and go to Sakura's bedroom.

page12.text:
"Thank goodness. You came, Senpai."
In bed,
Sakura sees my face and makes a slightly pained sigh.

page13.text: "Of course I came, silly. You fainted. I'd come for you no matter where you are. Tohsaka beat me to it first, but it's my job to look after you when you're sick."

page14.text:
I take a seat on the chair next to her bed.
Sakura does her best to make eye contact from where she's lying.

page15.text:
"So, how are you feeling? Tohsaka wouldn't tell me anything."
"Oh, really? She didn't tell you?"

page16.text:
"Nope. She said to ask you everything. I guess she was being considerate."
"Hehe. You look a little happy, Senpai. I've wondered this for a while, but you like the way my sister is strict on you sometimes, don't you?"

page17.text:
"A-as if!
Tohsaka's got a good head on her shoulders, but I couldn't take it if she were like that all the time! Besides, at times like these, it's that obvious consideration that keeps us sane. That goes for me and you."

page18.text:
Sakura nods with a smile.
Her expression looks so content, it makes me feel a little relieved.

page19.text:
"Good, I feel better seeing you like this. What did Tohsaka say?"
"Um, that my stamina is getting worse, I'm malnourished, and that I have a light fever.
She also said that there's nothing to worry about as long as I'm sleeping enough, so I have to get bed rest all day."

page20.text:
...
Sakura's breathing sounds labored even as she says that.
...Is she having a hard time even when she's lying down?
It seems like she's trying to control her breathing so that I don't worry.

page21.text:
"Okay. Then keep lying down for now. Do you, um, have enough magical energy?"
"Uh...ah, y-yes! I'm doing all right on that front th-thanks to you!"

page22.text:
...
I feel myself blushing as I ask.
Still, it's something I need to be sure of, so I'll have to put up with it.

page23.text:
"I bet you'll feel better once you get something good to eat. Hang on, I'll put everything I got into making you lunch."
I roll up my sleeve reassuringly.
However...

page24.text:
"...I'm sorry. I should actually be the one cooking for you.
...If I could stand up, I'd at least be able to help you, but I can't. It's frustrating."
Apparently, they were hard words for Sakura to hear.

page25.text:
...
...That's right.
Sakura's worried about her role in our home.
She wants to at least live life, even if she can't do anything about our situation.
But she isn't even allowed to do simple things like cook anymore.

page26.text: "Just hang in there for now. When a sick person doesn't rest, they'll just get sicker. Don't you worry, I plan to ask you to cook three meals a day once you're all better. You'll regret that you didn't get any rest while you still could."

page27.text:
I jokingly tell Sakura what's in store for her.
...Yeah.
I'll let her have the kitchen for half a year, if that makes her happy.

page28.text:
"Really? You won't go back on that, will you?"
"Really. I'll behave for half a year, at least.
Oh, no, I'll help you when things get hard. You should at least let me work in front of the stove."
I've been standing in the kitchen for the last eight years, too.
I need to hold a frying pan in my hands at least once in a while to feel at ease.

page29.text:
"All right, it's a promise. Once I get better, please eat my food."
"Yeah. I'll make you as many promises as you want."

page30.text:
I stand up from the chair.
I shouldn't tire Sakura out with any more conversation.
We got to talk, and I confirmed that Sakura is safe.
Now I need to let her rest.

page31.text:
"I'll be back when it's lunch time, so try to sleep until then."
I leave her bedside.
Sakura nods without saying anything.

page32.text:
"Oh right, Sakura..."
As I reach for the doorknob, something occurs to me.

page33.text:
"Yes? What, Senpai?"
"I was just wondering why you were on the ground in front of the door.
You went to sleep in my room last night, right?"
I ask the question as casually as possible.
After a slight pause, she answers.
